canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether memory-system changes can be accepted, monitored, or rejected using paired statistical evidence, protected-slice checks, and stage-level diagnostic traces rather than aggregate accuracy alone.
D^2ACCI separates an inner runtime memory loop from an outer diagnostic-evolution loop that evaluates candidate memory changes and controls promotion, rollback, or feature-flagging.
Per-sample diagnostic state records raw evidence, stored memory, retrieved top-k items, filtering decisions, assembled context, generated output, and final judgment.
Paired baseline and candidate samples are partitioned into improved, regressed, both-wrong, and both-correct sets, and material failures are assigned to the earliest actionable stage.
The paper uses the failure-stage labels ingestion miss, retrieval miss, context-assembly error, constraint error, generation error, component hurt, and unresolved ambiguity.

The gate-replay contract first feature-flags incomplete reports, rejects statistically significant harm, feature-flags insufficient DCR, feature-flags inconclusive paired evidence, accepts with monitoring when a protected slice regresses beyond tolerance, and otherwise accepts positive paired evidence.
Protected slices are specified from benchmark category structure before gate evaluation, including examples such as multi-hop, temporal, and sensitive-preference slices.
MemStack separates L0 atomic facts, L1 topic rollups, L2 user profiles, and session memory so feature ablations map to distinct failure families.
MemStack traces record source IDs, memory IDs, top-k scores, filtered items, packed or dropped context, and the final prompt at stage boundaries.

D^2ACCI-Eval joins paired examples by stable IDs, computes aggregate and slice deltas, exports discordances, runs McNemar tests and bootstrap confidence intervals, and creates a root-cause audit queue.
Diagnostic Coverage Rate at threshold tau is the proportion of failures or discordances with at least tau actionable traced stages.

outcome.definition: Proportion of failures or discordances with at least tau actionable trace stages.

canonical_statement: The default gate uses DCR@3 with a pre-specified minimum coverage threshold of 0.90 and reports sensitivity at DCR@1, DCR@5, and DCR@6.
MemStack achieved 93.59% accuracy on the 1,540-question non-adversarial LoCoMo evaluation.
MemStack achieved 90.93% accuracy on the 500-question LongMemEval-S evaluation.
MemStack achieved 57.20% accuracy on 5,000 PersonaMem-V2 multiple-choice questions over 200 personas.
Removing BM25/RRF on LoCoMo changed accuracy by -0.41 percentage points, with p=0.4426 and a 95% bootstrap interval from -1.36 to 0.56 percentage points.
Supplement extraction improved LoCoMo accuracy by 2.71 percentage points, with p=0.0009 and a 95% bootstrap interval from 1.26 to 4.20 percentage points.
Removing BM25/RRF on LongMemEval changed accuracy by 1.00 percentage point, with p=0.4583 and a 95% bootstrap interval from -1.13 to 3.13 percentage points.
Session-memory retrieval improved LongMemEval accuracy by 3.67 percentage points, with p=0.0026 and a 95% bootstrap interval from 1.33 to 6.00 percentage points.
Forget Guard improved PersonaMem-V2 accuracy by 1.92 percentage points, with p=0.0030 and a 95% bootstrap interval from 0.64 to 3.18 percentage points.
On the 60-case audit packet, GPT-4o relabeling with enriched traces achieved fine-grained Cohen kappa of 0.571 against Human A.
On the same 60-case audit packet, result-only GPT-4o relabeling achieved fine-grained Cohen kappa of 0.258 against Human A.
Human B achieved fine-grained Cohen kappa of 0.674 against Human A on the 60-case pre-adjudication audit packet.
LoCoMo No-BM25/RRF discordances achieved 99.21% DCR@3.
LoCoMo No-Supplement cases achieved 99.47% DCR@3.
LongMemEval No-Session cases achieved 98.63% DCR@3.
PersonaMem-V2 No-Forget-Guard cases achieved 100.00% DCR@3.
The 110-example LoCoMo result-only diagnostic check achieved 0% DCR@3.
Among 2,140 wrong PersonaMem-V2 cases, generation or option-scoring accounted for 1223 cases (57.1%).

canonical_statement: Deterministic gate replay over LoCoMo iterations t0 through t5 reproduced all five human-in-the-loop decisions, including rejection of the aggressive over-merge change.
An over-merge threshold of 0.75 was archived as an anti-pattern because it collapsed distinct facts into one memory representation, and the change was reverted.
An option-aware filter was archived as distractor amplification because retrieval surfaced distractor evidence, and the intervention was rejected.
A gated expansion that changed PersonaMem-V2 accuracy from 57.34% to 57.24% was retained only behind slice gating because it recovered some targets while adding off-target noise.
Published external benchmark numbers are not fully normalized same-stack baselines because answer models, judge prompts, and retrieval budgets differ.
Cross-benchmark replication of some ablations, including No Session on LoCoMo, was not complete in this preprint.

The paper identifies online evaluation, cross-stack comparisons, and automated trace verification as future extensions, so the reported evidence is primarily benchmark-based and current trace auditing is not fully automated.

The authors conclude that memory-system iteration should preserve paired statistical evidence, protected-slice monitoring, and stage-level traces so improvements can be distinguished from null or regressive changes.
The authors state that D^2ACCI can be applied to other memory stacks that emit stable sample identifiers and comparable stage traces.
